note: NECO Biology Paper III round 1: fresh SSCE-standard items with Nigerian examples, near-duplicate scanned against the JAMB and WAEC banks. Cell biology, nutrition, transport, respiration, excretion, support, coordination, reproduction, genetics, ecology, diseases and practical skills.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The basic structural and functional unit of living organisms is the
questions.explanation: All living things are made of cells, the smallest unit of life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which organelle does aerobic respiration mainly take place?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and energy release.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cell walls are found mainly in
questions.explanation: Plant cells have cellulose cell walls; animal cells do not.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which part of the cell controls all its activities?
questions.explanation: The nucleus carries the genetic material that directs cell activity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The green pigment found in chloroplasts is called
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll traps light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A membrane that lets some molecules through while blocking others is said to be
questions.explanation: A partially permeable membrane permits some molecules but blocks others.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: On which organelles are amino acids joined into proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which structure gives a plant cell its rigid shape?
questions.explanation: The cellulose cell wall is rigid and maintains cell shape.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The two daughter cells produced by mitosis are always
questions.B: half the chromosome number of the parent
questions.D: genetically identical to the parent cell
questions.explanation: Mitosis is an exact division: the daughter cells carry the same chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number of a cell by
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces gametes with half the diploid number.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which stage of mitosis do chromosomes arrange at the equator of the cell?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes line up along the equator during metaphase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Crossing over of genetic material occurs during
questions.explanation: Chromatids exchange segments in prophase I, giving new gene combinations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Body (somatic) cells divide by
questions.explanation: Growth and repair of body tissues happen by mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide, water, chlorophyll and
questions.explanation: Light energy trapped by chlorophyll drives photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During photosynthesis, the oxygen given off comes from the
questions.explanation: Water is photolysed; its oxygen is released as a by-product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Yellowing of leaves (chlorosis) in plants is caused by deficiency of
questions.explanation: Magnesium is needed to make chlorophyll; its lack causes yellowing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Saliva contains an enzyme that digests cooked starch. The enzyme is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch into maltose in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the
questions.explanation: Bile made in the liver is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The final products of protein digestion are
questions.explanation: Proteins are digested to amino acids, which the blood absorbs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Most water absorption in the alimentary canal takes place in the
questions.explanation: The colon reabsorbs most of the water from the food residue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tapeworm obtains its food by
questions.B: biting the intestinal wall with hooks
questions.D: absorbing digested food through its body surface
questions.explanation: The tapeworm's whole surface absorbs the host's digested food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Water and dissolved mineral salts are transported in a plant through the
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals from root to leaf.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The loss of water vapour from leaves occurs mainly through the
questions.explanation: Most transpiration happens through stomatal pores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Manufactured food is translocated in flowering plants through the
questions.explanation: Phloem sieve tubes move sucrose and other food materials.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person with blood group O is described as a universal
questions.explanation: Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigens, so most people can receive them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood is carried AWAY from the heart in the
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pigment that carries oxygen in red blood cells is
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin combines reversibly with oxygen to transport it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Transpiration pull is strongest when the weather is
questions.explanation: Dry moving air raises the evaporation rate, pulling more water up.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol and
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The gas released during aerobic respiration is
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose to carbon dioxide and water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Energy released during respiration is stored in cells as
questions.explanation: ATP is the energy currency that cells spend for their work.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The tired, aching feeling in muscles after a long race is due to the build-up of
questions.explanation: Short of oxygen, muscles ferment glucose to lactic acid, causing fatigue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which group of organisms respire anaerobically in mud?
questions.explanation: Certain anaerobic bacteria in mud respire without oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The excretory organs of insects are the
questions.explanation: Insects excrete nitrogenous waste through Malpighian tubules into the gut.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Each kidney contains about a million tiny filtering units called the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter the blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood is filtered under pressure into the kidney's
questions.explanation: Blood is filtered under pressure from the glomerulus into the Bowman's capsule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The lungs excrete
questions.explanation: Breathing out removes carbon dioxide and water from respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The liver helps excretion by
questions.D: storing bile salts for later use
questions.explanation: The liver destroys aged red cells and excretes the pigments in bile.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Skull, vertebral column and rib cage together make up the
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton forms the central axis of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Support in soft herbaceous plants is mainly due to
questions.explanation: Water pressure in cells keeps soft stems firm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The elbow can bend and straighten but cannot rotate. It is a
questions.explanation: Hinge joints bend and straighten in one plane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ligaments join
questions.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments hold bones together at joints.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The vertebral column of a mammal is divided into how many regions?
questions.explanation: Cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral and caudal regions make five.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sclerenchyma fibres strengthen a plant because their walls are
questions.explanation: Lignin-deposited walls of sclerenchyma give rigid support.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
questions.explanation: Neurones transmit nerve impulses; they are the units of the nervous system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Reflex actions such as withdrawing the hand from a hot object are coordinated in the
questions.explanation: Reflex arcs pass through the spinal cord for a fast response.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the brain that controls body balance and posture is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscle action and balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The tiny gap across which a nerve impulse passes from one neurone to the next is the
questions.explanation: At the synapse, chemicals carry the impulse across the gap.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The iris of the eye controls the size of the
questions.explanation: Iris muscles widen or narrow the pupil to control light entry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Long-sightedness is corrected by wearing
questions.explanation: A convex lens converges light so the image focuses on the retina.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insulin is produced by the
questions.explanation: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which hormone is responsible for the development of female secondary sexual characters?
questions.explanation: Oestrogen drives female secondary characters at puberty.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Adrenaline secretion increases the
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for action: faster heart and more blood sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Auxins in plants promote
questions.explanation: Auxins lengthen cells, bending shoots toward light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Diabetes mellitus results when the body cannot produce enough
questions.explanation: Without insulin, blood glucose cannot be controlled or stored.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After landing on the stigma, pollen grains germinate. Pollination is the act of transferring pollen from the anther to the
questions.explanation: Pollen must land on a compatible stigma before fertilisation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fertilisation in a flowering plant occurs in the
questions.explanation: The male gamete fuses with the egg inside the ovule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Food, oxygen and wastes pass between mother and foetus across the
questions.A: protect the foetus from all drugs
questions.C: produce the foetus's blood cells alone
questions.explanation: The placenta is the exchange surface for food, oxygen and wastes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: External fertilisation is common in
questions.explanation: Fish and frogs shed gametes into water where fertilisation occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Germination in a bean seedling is described as epigeal because the
questions.D: cotyledons are carried above the soil surface
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the hypocotyl lifts the cotyledons above ground.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The average length of the human menstrual cycle is about
questions.explanation: A typical cycle runs about twenty-eight days from one period to the next.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In mammals, the fertilised egg implants in the
questions.explanation: The blastocyst embeds in the uterine wall where it develops.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mendel's first law of genetics is the law of
questions.explanation: Allelic pairs separate during gamete formation; this is segregation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt) are crossed. The expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is
questions.explanation: Tt x Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: three tall to one short.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The genetic make-up of an organism is called its
questions.explanation: Genotype is the gene combination; phenotype is what is seen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Whether a baby is a boy or a girl depends on the
questions.explanation: The mother always gives an X; the father's sperm gives X or Y.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man with genotype AA marries a woman with genotype aa (sickle-cell). Their children will be
questions.explanation: Every child receives A from the father and a from the mother: Aa carriers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sickle-cell anaemia arises from a change in a gene. Such a change is called a
questions.explanation: A sudden change in gene structure is a mutation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Down's syndrome results from a chromosomal abnormality called
questions.explanation: Failure of chromosome 21 to separate gives an extra copy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The linear path through which energy flows in an ecosystem is called a
questions.explanation: A food chain shows who eats whom, passing energy along.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → snake, the grasshopper is a
questions.explanation: Herbivores feeding directly on producers are primary consumers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The association between Rhizobium bacteria and legume roots, where both organisms benefit, is called
questions.explanation: Both partners gain: the plant gets nitrogen, the bacteria get food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sleeping sickness (trypanosomiasis) is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly carries the trypanosome parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Decomposers are important in an ecosystem because they
questions.A: recycle nutrients back to the soil
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi break down dead matter, returning nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Guinea worm infection is contracted by drinking water containing
questions.explanation: The guinea worm larva lives inside Cyclops before infecting humans.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A population is best defined as organisms of
questions.A: the same species living together in the same area
questions.B: different species in the same habitat
questions.C: the same species anywhere on earth
questions.explanation: Population = one species, one place, one time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which gas is the largest contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from burning fuels traps the most heat radiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of the
questions.explanation: Only the female Anopheles mosquito carries the malaria parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is viral; cholera and typhoid are bacterial, ringworm fungal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Immunity gained by suffering and recovering from a disease is
questions.explanation: Your own antibodies made after infection give natural active immunity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: AIDS is caused by
questions.explanation: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus attacks the immune system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vaccination gives protection by stimulating the body to produce
questions.explanation: Vaccines carry weakened antigens that trigger antibody production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bleeding gums and slow wound healing are signs of scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leaf is boiled in alcohol during the starch test in order to
questions.explanation: Alcohol decolourises the leaf so the iodine colour can show.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fehling's solutions A and B are used to test for
questions.explanation: Reducing sugars turn Fehling's brick-red on warming.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The biuret test gives a violet colour in the presence of
questions.explanation: Protein plus sodium hydroxide and copper sulfate turns violet.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A destarched plant is used in photosynthesis experiments so that
questions.A: any starch found afterwards must have formed during the experiment
questions.B: all the leaves turn blue-black at the same time
questions.C: the plant will need much less water during the test
questions.D: the green chlorophyll is completely removed from every leaf
questions.explanation: Keeping the plant in darkness uses up stored starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: To see the details of an onion cell clearly, a student should use a
questions.explanation: Microscopes magnify cells many times beyond a hand lens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In an experiment to show that carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis, the leaf half enclosed with sodium hydroxide tests
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide, so no starch forms on that half.
